Chest.name: Bench Press
Chest.imageAlt: Chest muscles used during the bench press
howToPerform: Lie flat on the bench with your eyes positioned underneath the bar. Place your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and grip the bar firmly. Keep your feet planted on the floor and your upper back against the bench.

Unrack the bar and bring it over your chest with your arms extended. Lower the bar under control toward the middle of your chest while keeping your elbows slightly tucked. Press the bar back up until your arms are extended without excessively flaring your elbows.
secondaryMuscles: Triceps brachii (Triceps) and anterior deltoids (Front Delt)

Chest.name: Cable Chest Fly
Chest.imageAlt: Chest muscles used during the cable chest fly
howToPerform: Set the cable pulleys around chest height and grasp one handle in each hand. Step forward into a stable stance and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a controlled arc while keeping your elbows slightly bent. Slowly return your arms to the starting position while maintaining tension in your chest.
secondaryMuscles: Anterior deltoid (Front Delt)

Chest.name: Dip
Chest.imageAlt: Chest muscles used during the dip
howToPerform: Grip the parallel bars firmly and support your body with your arms extended. Lean your torso slightly forward while keeping your feet behind you.

Lower your body under control by bending your elbows and allowing your chest to move between the bars. Press through your hands to return to the starting position while keeping your movement controlled.
secondaryMuscles: Triceps brachii (Triceps) and anterior deltoid (Front Delt)

Chest.name: Incline Bench Press
Chest.imageAlt: Chest muscles used during the incline bench press
howToPerform: Set the bench to a moderate incline and lie back with your feet planted firmly on the floor. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and keep your upper back supported against the bench.
Unrack the bar and lower it under control toward the upper portion of your chest. Keep your elbows slightly tucked as you press the bar upward until your arms are extended.
secondaryMuscles: Anterior deltoid (Front Delt) and triceps brachii (Triceps)

Chest.name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
Chest.imageAlt: Chest muscles used during the incline dumbbell bench press
howToPerform: Set the bench to a moderate incline and sit with a dumbbell in each hand. Position the dumbbells near your shoulders and keep your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Press both dumbbells upward while keeping them controlled and aligned over your chest. Lower them slowly toward the sides of your upper chest before pressing them back up.
secondaryMuscles: Anterior deltoid (Front Delt) and triceps brachii (Triceps)

Chest.name: Pec Deck
Chest.imageAlt: Chest muscles used during the pec deck
howToPerform: Sit upright on the pec deck with your back against the pad. Position your arms on the machine's handles or pads and keep your feet planted firmly on the floor.

Bring the handles together in front of your chest while keeping a slight bend in your elbows. Slowly return the handles to the starting position without allowing the weight to pull your arms back too quickly.
secondaryMuscles: Anterior deltoid (Front Delt)

Back.name: Bent-Over Row
Back.imageAlt: Back muscles used during the bent-over row
howToPerform: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell with a firm grip. Hinge at your hips while keeping your back neutral and your knees slightly bent.
Pull the barbell toward your lower chest or upper abdomen by driving your elbows backward. Squeeze your back at the top of the movement, then lower the barbell under control.
secondaryMuscles: Rhomboid major (Rhomboids), trapezius (Traps), posterior deltoid (Rear Delt), and biceps brachii (Biceps)

Back.name: Cable Row
Back.imageAlt: Back muscles used during the cable row
howToPerform: Sit at the cable row station with your feet supported and your knees slightly bent. Grip the handle with both hands and sit upright with your arms extended.

Pull the handle toward your lower chest or upper abdomen by driving your elbows backward. Squeeze your back at the end of the movement, then slowly extend your arms to return to the starting position.
secondaryMuscles: Rhomboid major (Rhomboids), trapezius (Traps), posterior deltoid (Rear Delt), and biceps brachii (Biceps)

Back.name: Deadlift
Back.imageAlt: Back muscles used during the deadlift
howToPerform: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and the barbell over the middle of your feet. Hinge at your hips and bend your knees until you can grip the bar while keeping your back neutral.

Brace your core and drive through the floor as you extend your knees and hips. Keep the bar close to your body as you stand tall, then hinge at the hips and bend your knees to lower the bar under control.
secondaryMuscles: Gluteus maximus (Glutes), hamstrings (Hamstrings), trapezius (Traps), and latissimus dorsi (Lats)

Back.name: Lat Pulldown
Back.imageAlt: Back muscles used during the lat pulldown
howToPerform: Sit at the lat pulldown machine and secure your legs under the pads. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart with your palms facing forward.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back. Pause briefly, then slowly allow the bar to return to the starting position while keeping control of the weight.
secondaryMuscles: Biceps brachii (Biceps), trapezius (Traps), and posterior deltoid (Rear Delt)

Back.name: Pull-Up
Back.imageAlt: Back muscles used during the pull-up
howToPerform: Grip the pull-up bar slightly wider than shoulder-width apart with your palms facing away from you. Hang from the bar with your arms extended and your core engaged.
Pull your body upward by driving your elbows down toward your sides. Continue until your chin clears the bar, then lower yourself under control until your arms are extended again.
secondaryMuscles: Biceps brachii (Biceps), trapezius (Traps), and posterior deltoid (Rear Delt)

Back.name: T-Bar Row
Back.imageAlt: Back muscles used during the T-bar row
howToPerform: Stand over the bar with your feet about shoulder-width apart. Bend at your hips and knees while keeping your back neutral, then grip the handles firmly.
Pull the weight toward your torso by driving your elbows back. Keep your chest controlled and your spine neutral throughout the movement, then lower the weight slowly until your arms are extended.
secondaryMuscles: Rhomboid major (Rhomboids), trapezius (Traps), posterior deltoid (Rear Delt), and biceps brachii (Biceps)

Arms.name: Bayesian Curl
Arms.imageAlt: Arm muscles used during the Bayesian curl
howToPerform: Stand in front of a low cable pulley with your working arm behind your body. Grip the handle with your palm facing upward and keep your upper arm slightly behind your torso.
Curl the handle forward and upward while keeping your upper arm behind your body. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then slowly extend your elbow back to the starting position.
secondaryMuscles: Brachialis (Biceps) and brachioradialis (Forearms)

Arms.name: Dumbbell Curl
Arms.imageAlt: Arm muscles used during the dumbbell curl
howToPerform: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand and your arms at your sides. Keep your elbows close to your torso and your palms facing forward.
Curl the dumbbells upward by bending your elbows while keeping your upper arms stationary. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly.
secondaryMuscles: Brachialis (Biceps) and brachioradialis (Forearms)

Arms.name: EZ-Bar Curl
Arms.imageAlt: Arm muscles used during the EZ-bar curl
howToPerform: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart while holding the EZ-bar with a comfortable underhand grip. Keep your elbows close to your sides and your torso upright.
Curl the bar upward by bending your elbows without swinging your torso. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower the bar under control to the starting position.
secondaryMuscles: Brachialis (Biceps) and brachioradialis (Forearms)

Arms.name: Preacher Curl
Arms.imageAlt: Arm muscles used during the preacher curl
howToPerform: Sit at the preacher curl bench and position your upper arms securely against the pad. Grip the bar or dumbbells with your palms facing upward.
Curl the weight upward by bending your elbows while keeping your upper arms against the pad. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower the weight slowly until your arms are nearly straight.
secondaryMuscles: Brachialis (Biceps) and brachioradialis (Forearms)

Arms.name: Rope Hammer Curl
Arms.imageAlt: Arm muscles used during the rope hammer curl
howToPerform: Stand facing a low cable pulley and grip the rope with a neutral, palms-facing-inward grip. Keep your elbows close to your sides and your torso stable.
Curl the rope upward by bending your elbows while keeping your upper arms stationary. Squeeze your arms at the top, then lower the rope slowly to the starting position.
secondaryMuscles: Biceps brachii (Biceps) and brachioradialis (Forearms)

Arms.name: Skull Crusher
Arms.imageAlt: Arm muscles used during the skull crusher
howToPerform: Lie flat on a bench while holding a barbell or dumbbells above your chest with your arms extended. Keep your upper arms relatively stationary.
Bend your elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead or slightly behind your head. Extend your elbows to press the weight back to the starting position.
secondaryMuscles: Anconeus (Triceps)

Arms.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
Arms.imageAlt: Arm muscles used during the overhead tricep extension
howToPerform: Hold the weight overhead with your elbows pointed forward and your upper arms kept close to your head. Brace your core and keep your torso stable.
Bend your elbows to lower the weight behind your head while keeping your upper arms relatively stationary. Extend your elbows to return the weight to the starting position.
secondaryMuscles: Anconeus (Triceps)

Arms.name: Tricep Pushdown
Arms.imageAlt: Arm muscles used during the tricep pushdown
howToPerform: Stand facing the cable machine and grip the attachment with your hands. Keep your elbows close to your sides and brace your core.
Push the attachment downward by extending your elbows until your arms are straight. Squeeze your triceps at the bottom, then slowly return the attachment to the starting position.
secondaryMuscles: Anconeus (Triceps)

Legs.name: Calf Raise
Legs.imageAlt: Calf muscles used during the calf raise
howToPerform: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and position yourself securely on the calf raise machine or platform. Keep your knees slightly bent and your core stable.
Raise your heels as high as possible by pressing through the balls of your feet. Pause at the top, then lower your heels under control to achieve a full stretch.
secondaryMuscles: Soleus (Calves)

Legs.name: Leg Curl
Legs.imageAlt: Leg muscles used during the leg curl
howToPerform: Position yourself securely in the leg curl machine with your knees aligned with the machine's pivot point. Place the lower part of your legs against the resistance pad.
Curl your lower legs toward your body by bending your knees. Squeeze your hamstrings at the end of the movement, then slowly return your legs to the starting position.
secondaryMuscles: Gastrocnemius (Calves)

Legs.name: Leg Extension
Legs.imageAlt: Leg muscles used during the leg extension
howToPerform: Sit in the leg extension machine with your back against the pad and your knees aligned with the machine's pivot point. Position the lower pad against the front of your lower legs.
Extend your knees to raise the pad while keeping your hips and back against the seat. Squeeze your quadriceps at the top, then lower the weight slowly back to the starting position.
secondaryMuscles: Tensor fasciae latae (Hip Flexor)

Legs.name: Leg Press
Legs.imageAlt: Leg muscles used during the leg press
howToPerform: Sit in the leg press machine with your back and hips firmly against the pad. Place your feet about shoulder-width apart on the platform and keep your knees aligned with your feet.

Lower the platform by bending your knees and hips under control. Stop before your lower back lifts from the pad, then press through your feet to extend your legs without locking your knees aggressively.
secondaryMuscles: Gluteus maximus (Glutes), hamstrings (Hamstrings), and adductor magnus (Adductors)

Legs.name: Romanian Deadlift
Legs.imageAlt: Leg muscles used during the Romanian deadlift
howToPerform: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart while holding the barbell in front of your thighs. Keep your knees slightly bent and brace your core.
Push your hips backward while lowering the bar close to your legs. Continue until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, then drive your hips forward to return to standing.
secondaryMuscles: Erector spinae (Lower Back), adductor magnus (Adductors), and trapezius (Traps)

Legs.name: Squat
Legs.imageAlt: Leg muscles used during the squat
howToPerform: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart with the barbell resting across your upper back. Brace your core and keep your chest controlled as you prepare to squat.
Bend your knees and hips to lower your body while keeping your feet planted on the floor. Descend to a comfortable depth, then drive through the floor to return to the starting position.
secondaryMuscles: Hamstrings (Hamstrings), adductor magnus (Adductors), and erector spinae (Lower Back)

Shoulders.name: Barbell Shoulder Press
Shoulders.imageAlt: Shoulder muscles used during the barbell shoulder press
howToPerform: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell at about shoulder height. Keep your core braced and your elbows positioned slightly in front of the bar.
Press the barbell overhead until your arms are extended without excessively leaning backward. Lower the bar under control back to shoulder height.
primaryMuscles: Anterior deltoid (Front Delt) and medial deltoid (Side Delt)
secondaryMuscles: Triceps brachii (Triceps), upper trapezius (Upper Traps), and pectoralis major (Upper Chest)

Shoulders.name: Cable Lateral Raise
Shoulders.imageAlt: Shoulder muscles used during the cable lateral raise
howToPerform: Stand beside a low cable pulley and hold the handle with the hand farthest from the machine. Keep your arm slightly bent and your torso stable.
Raise your arm out to the side until it is about parallel with the floor. Lower the handle slowly and maintain control throughout the movement.
secondaryMuscles: Anterior deltoid (Front Delt) and posterior deltoid (Rear Delt)

Shoulders.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
Shoulders.imageAlt: Shoulder muscles used during the dumbbell shoulder press
howToPerform: Sit or stand with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height. Keep your core braced and your wrists stacked over your elbows.
Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are extended. Lower the dumbbells under control back to shoulder height while maintaining a stable torso.
primaryMuscles: Anterior deltoid (Front Delt) and medial deltoid (Side Delt)
secondaryMuscles: Triceps brachii (Triceps), upper trapezius (Upper Traps), and pectoralis major (Upper Chest)

Shoulders.name: Face Pull
Shoulders.imageAlt: Shoulder muscles used during the face pull
howToPerform: Set a cable pulley around upper-chest or face height and attach a rope. Grip the rope with both hands and step back until there is tension in the cable.
Pull the rope toward your face while driving your elbows outward and rotating your hands back. Squeeze your upper back and shoulders, then return the rope under control.
secondaryMuscles: Infraspinatus (Rotator Cuff), teres minor (Rotator Cuff), and trapezius (Traps)

Shoulders.name: Lateral Raise
Shoulders.imageAlt: Shoulder muscles used during the lateral raise
howToPerform: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and maintain a controlled posture.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they are about parallel with the floor. Pause briefly, then lower the dumbbells slowly back to your sides.
secondaryMuscles: Anterior deltoid (Front Delt) and posterior deltoid (Rear Delt)

Shoulders.name: Reverse Cable Fly
Shoulders.imageAlt: Shoulder muscles used during the reverse cable fly
howToPerform: Set the cable pulleys around shoulder height and stand between them. Grip the opposite handle with each hand and keep your arms slightly bent.
Pull your arms outward and backward in a wide arc until your arms are roughly in line with your body. Squeeze your rear shoulders, then return to the starting position under control.
secondaryMuscles: Trapezius (Traps), rhomboid major (Rhomboids), and infraspinatus (Rotator Cuff)
